# dla_wwaddw

> Add a vector to a doubled-single precision accumulator (X, Y).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaWwaddw from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dla_wwaddw';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dla_wwaddw( N, x, strideX, y, strideY, w, strideW ) → Float64Array
```

Adds a vector `W` to a doubled-single precision accumulator `(X, Y)` in place.

The accumulator's high-order part is stored in `X` and low-order part in `Y`
so that `X[i] + Y[i]` approximates the running sum with extra precision.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements in `X`, `Y`, and `W` |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · High-order part of the accumulator (modified in place) |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Low-order part of the accumulator (modified in place) |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Vector to be added |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The length of vectors X, Y, and W.
- `x`: The first part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `y`: The second part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `w`: The vector to be added.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dla_wwaddw.ndarray(
    N,
    x, strideX, offsetX,
    y, strideY, offsetY,
    w, strideW, offsetW
) → Float64Array
```

Adds a vector `W` to a doubled-single precision accumulator `(X, Y)` in place.
using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements in `X`, `Y`, and `W` |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · High-order part of the accumulator (modified in place) |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Low-order part of the accumulator (modified in place) |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Vector to be added |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The length of vectors X, Y, and W.
- `x`: The first part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `y`: The second part of the doubled-single accumulation vector.
- `w`: The vector to be added.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dla_wwaddw()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLA_WWADDW`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dla_wwaddw.f).
-   The `(s + s) - s` rounding step in the inner loop is **not** a no-op in IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic. It extracts the rounded high-order part of `x[i] + w[i]`, with the truncated low-order bits pushed into the compensation term `y[i]`.
-   This routine is a leaf LAPACK helper used by iterative refinement extended routines (`dgerfsx`, `dsyrfsx`, `dporfsx`, etc.) for extra-precise accumulation.
-   Quick return when `N == 0`: all arrays are left untouched.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable camelcase */

import uniform from '@stdlib/random/array/uniform/lib/index.js';
import dla_wwaddw from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dla_wwaddw';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};

const N = 5;
const x = uniform( N, -10.0, 10.0, opts );
const y = uniform( N, -1.0e-10, 1.0e-10, opts );
const w = uniform( N, -1.0, 1.0, opts );

dla_wwaddw( N, x, 1, y, 1, w, 1 );
console.log( x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( y ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLA_WWADDW`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLA\_WWADDW adds a vector W into a doubled-single vector (X, Y).

This works for all extant IBM's hex and binary floating point arithmetic, but not for decimal.

</section>
